draft.title: Percentage increase and decrease
card: A discount is a percentage decrease. A mark-up is a percentage increase. To change an amount in one step, multiply by a single factor. The factor is the new amount as a decimal fraction of the original.
Add the percentage to 100%, then write it as a decimal. A mark-up of 15% is \(100\% + 15\% = 115\%\), so the factor is 1.15.
Take the percentage from 100%, then write it as a decimal. A 20% discount is \(100\% - 20\% = 80\%\), so the factor is 0.8.
Adding 10% GST is an increase of 10%, so multiply by 1.1. A $60 jacket with GST added costs \(60 \times 1.1 = \$66\).
draft.remember: Increase: 100% plus the change. Decrease: 100% minus the change. Then multiply.

a.q: A shop gives 30% off. Which factor do you multiply the price by?
a.why: A 30% decrease leaves \(100\% - 30\% = 70\%\), which is 0.7. The factor 0.3 is tempting, but multiplying by 0.3 leaves only 30% of the amount, so it is a 70% decrease.
a.clue: Work out what percentage is left after the decrease.

b.q: A gym fee is $40 a week before a 15% mark-up. What is the new weekly fee?
b.why: The factor is 1.15, so \(40 \times 1.15 = \$46\). The answer $6 is only the increase (15% of 40), not the new fee.
b.clue: The question asks for the new fee, not the size of the rise.
